# dsh-plugin-moss-tts
简体中文 · Version **0.1.1** · Apache-2.0 · Engine repo

Local text-to-speech for DeepSeek Harness, powered by the MOSS-TTS-Nano-100M C++ CPU engine.
Everyth

ing is synthesized on this machine; text never leaves it, and the weights are installed
once and sha
red with the CLI and the web playground.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Requirements
| Item | Requirement |

| DeepSeek Harness | 0.2.1-rc or newer (client slot contract) |
| OS | Windows x64 (the engine ships

for that platform only) |
| Disk | ~170 MB (engine + weights), installed once |
## Install
**Desktop app**: sidebar **Plugins** → **Add plugin** → paste
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**CLI profile** (a profile the desktop app does not own):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**Restart DSH** afterwards. You get a "Moss Speech" settings page, a speaker toggle at the left
of t
he composer, a read button on every assistant reply, and five `moss_tts_*` tools.
> Installing from a local checkout: `dsh plugin --profile <name> add D:\path\to\dsh-plugin-moss-tts`
> (an absolute path is required).
## First run: install the engine

Open **Settings → Moss Speech → Download engine**. The plugin fetches
`MossTTS-win-x64-full.zip` (~1

60 MB) from the
engine releases, verifies it against the
release's `sha256sums.txt`, and extracts it
into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MossTTS`.

- Already installed via the CLI or the web playground? It is reused; nothing is downloaded twice.
-

Downloads resume after an interruption; cancel removes only the partial file.
- **Follows your syste

m proxy**: `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` first, then the Windows Internet
settings (`ProxyEnable` + `

ProxyServer`, via a CONNECT tunnel). A machine whose browser can open
GitHub needs no extra configur

ation; set `NO_PROXY=*` to force direct connections.
- Behind a blocked network, point `engineUrl` +

`engineSha256` at a mirror in the plugin config,
or set `autoDownload: false` and manage the instal

256` at a mirror in the plugin config,
or set `autoDownload: false` and manage the install yourself.
## Usage
| Entry point | What it does |
| 🔊 left of the composer | Auto-read. Reads each reply when it settles; while speaking the same butt

on is ⏹ and stops it |
| 🔊 on a reply | Reads that reply only (whole text, ignores the auto-read lim

it) |
| Settings → Moss Speech | Voice, auto-read limit, skip code blocks, preview, engine state and

paths |
| `moss_tts_say` | Agent-initiated speech (plays locally, or `save_to` writes a WAV) |
| `m
oss_tts_voices` / `moss_tts_stop` / `moss_tts_clone` / `moss_tts_engine` | Voices / stop / clone a v
oice / engine status and install |

Markdown is cleaned before speaking: fenced code and tables are skipped, links keep their text,
head

ing and list markers are stripped, and long replies are cut on a sentence boundary at the
auto-read
limit (default 1500 characters, 0 = unlimited).
## Privacy

- Synthesis is fully local: no network, no uploaded text, no telemetry.
- The only outbound traffic

is the engine download you trigger from the settings page.
- Cloned voices live under `%LOCALAPPDATA
%\MossTTS\userdata\voices\user\`.
## How it relates to the CLI and the web playground
All three run the same `moss_tts.exe`, the same weights and the same data directory:

- CLI: `moss_tts.exe --text "hello" --out hello.wav`
- Web playground: double-click `moss_tts.exe` →

`http://127.0.0.1:8759/`
- This plugin: no port; it spawns the resident engine over `--stdio`

Engine and plugin version independently: `engine.json` pins a release, falls back to the latest
one
when that tag is gone, and always verifies the release's `sha256sums.txt`.
## Uninstall

In the desktop app, remove it from the sidebar **Plugins** page. For a CLI-managed profile:
`dsh plu
gin --profile <name> remove dsh-plugin-moss-tts`.

The weights are left in place (the CLI and the web playground still use them). Delete
`%LOCALAPPDATA
%\MossTTS` to remove them too.
## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Fix |
| Settings keeps showing "not installed" | Press "Re-check"; verify `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MossTTS\moss_tts

.exe` and `models\` exist |
| Download fails / hash mismatch | Usually a proxy rewriting the body. R

etry once; if it persists, set `engineUrl` + `engineSha256` in the plugin config |
| "Ready" but sil
ent | The tab is muted, or the output device is wrong; click anywhere in the page once so the browse

r allows playback |
| Long replies are cut short | The auto-read limit (1500 chars) — raise it in se

ttings, or use the reply's own read button |
| Plugin does not appear | DSH must be restarted; `dsh
--profile desktop --dump-config` should contain a row `id: moss-tts` |
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Host contract (verified against DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 on the development machine): `dsh.bundle.patch`
inser

ts one loader row for the host half; `dsh.client.platform = "web"` plus
`exports["./client"]` load t

he browser half; the host registers routes through
`ctx.get('webServer').register` and the client re

gisters slots through `ctx.slots.inject`.
Nothing is imported from the host packages — tool definiti

ons are plain objects with standard
JSON Schema.
## License

Apache-2.0. Model weights come from MOSS-TTS-Nano-100M (Apache-2.0) and are converted to the
engine'

s container format by the engine repo; this package ships **no** weights or binaries and
downloads t
hem at runtime. See NOTICE.
